name: Hannah's Lambing Notebook
desc: A school exercise book, spattered. Dates, ewes, a column headed 'Dad says' and a column headed 'Actually'. The second column is winning.

name: Dale's Old Crook
desc: An ash crook worn pale where one hand held it for forty years. Dale did not want it left in the farmhouse porch. 'Somebody ought to carry it,' he said.

name: Curlew Tally Sheet
desc: A ranger's tally sheet for Moor Farm: nine pairs of curlew in a neat column, five in the last. Somebody has drawn a very small bird in the margin.

name: Slate from the Hall Roof
desc: A spare Caithness slate from the first batch for the hall roof, signed on the back in pencil by about forty people, one of whom drew a very small turbine.

name: Greenshank Feather
desc: A grey-brown feather, moulted and not taken, found on the ridge by the warden. 'They were here again this year,' says the card.

name: A Page of Hall Minutes
desc: The minute of the meeting that moved the turbines. Four people abstained, three said 'aye' and one wrote 'under protest' and then crossed it out.

name: Bethania Door Key
desc: A black iron chapel key, heavy as a spanner. The chapel has a new key now, brass, for the flats. This one hung in the vestry for about a century.

name: Roof Fund Thermometer Card
desc: A painted card thermometer from the chapel porch, red up to forty per cent. Mrs Pugh's sister did the lettering. Someone has added a very small ladder.

name: Two Keys on One Ring
desc: One brass, one iron, on a loop of string. Flats at the back, chapel at the front. The label says 'do not lose either'.

name: The Snug Latch
desc: A brass latch off the snug door, which has gone. Pádraig kept it. 'For the next one who wants a bit of privacy,' says the label, in biro.

name: Co-op Share No. 1
desc: A share certificate in a pub co-op, number one of three hundred and forty. The cheque stub has been framed. Pádraig has signed the back, and added 'cheap at the price'.

name: The Last Orders Bell
desc: A small brass bell that rang last orders for sixty years. The new management has a clock. Pádraig took the bell, and then, kindly, lent it to you.

name: The Rota Biscuit Tin
desc: A shortbread tin with eleven names on the lid in biro, and a twelfth space left blank. Margaret keeps it on the counter and says it has never been wrong.

name: The Old Brass Scales
desc: Maeve's brass parcel scales, with a set of weights that went missing in 1986 and came back in 1991. They are accurate to a gram, and have never been told.

name: A Sign: 'Back at 2'
desc: A hand-lettered card from the shutter of the old counter, the one that went up the week the cover fell through. Underneath, someone has written 'And we were'.

name: The Old Boat's Engine Plate
desc: A brass plate off the old boat's engine, polished, with a maker's name and a date from the year the boat came on the run. Magnie says she has earned a plate and a pension.

name: The Three-Day Timetable
desc: A laminated timetable: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. In pen across the top, in Eila's hand: 'Lorna says it is not a timetable, it is a sentence'.

name: The Old Lifebelt
desc: A cork-and-canvas lifebelt, painted with the name of the old boat in red. The new boat has a better one. Nobody could throw this one away.
